surfaces.name: Crush terminal UI (crush command, Bubble Tea)
Crush server and client/server mode (crush server, HTTP API)

claims.answer: Terminal client on macOS, Linux, Windows (PowerShell, WSL), Android terminals and BSDs via package managers and binaries; crush run for headless use; crush server exposes an HTTP API that other clients can attach to. No native desktop app, mobile app, browser UI or editor extension ships in this release.

desktop_os.answer: README feature list states terminal support on macOS, Linux and Windows (PowerShell and WSL) plus BSDs; release binaries for each.

mobile_apps.answer: No iOS or Android app; Android is only named as a supported terminal environment. Bounded search of README, cmd and ui found no mobile client.

browser.answer: Terminal UI only; the server exposes an API and docs page but no browser interface (internal/server endpoints and docs.html template only serve API documentation).

mobile_browser.answer: No browser UI to reach from a phone.

cli.answer: crush launches the TUI; run, session, stats, logs, models, login, projects and server subcommands.

editor_extensions.answer: Bounded search of the repo (terms vsix, vscode extension, jetbrains plugin) found no editor extension.

task_actions.answer: Start, steer (queued prompts), approve (permission dialog), review (diffs and modified files in sidebar) and resume sessions in the TUI; run supports --session/--continue.

notifications.answer: Native, OSC or bell notifications for permission requests and turn completion only while terminal unfocused; no push or mobile alerts.

cross_device_continuity.answer: Sessions persist in SQLite on the host and a shared crush server lets another client attach to the same workspace, but there is no hosted account or sync.

limitations: No browser, mobile or editor client; remote use means SSH to a terminal or a client/server attach.
No notifications beyond local native/OSC/bell alerts.

claims.answer: Crush embeds its own agent loop (via the fantasy provider layer) rather than launching other agent CLIs. Model providers are broad: Hyper, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Bedrock, Vertex, Azure, OpenRouter, Groq, xAI and others plus custom OpenAI- or Anthropic-compatible endpoints and local servers. Mixed-harness operation does not exist; subagents can use a different model but not a different harness.

harnesses.answer: One embedded harness (Crush itself); it does not start Claude Code, Codex or other agent CLIs. Bounded search of internal/agent and internal/cmd found no launch of third-party agent CLIs.

model_providers.answer: README lists about 20 provider environment variables (Hyper, Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel, Gemini, Z.ai, MiniMax, OpenRouter, Groq, Bedrock, Azure, Moonshot, xAI and more) and Catwalk-managed model lists.

custom_adapters.answer: Custom providers of type openai-compat, openai (responses) and anthropic via crushrc provider add or JSON config; local model discovery for Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp.

session_integration.answer: Crush embeds the harness: it runs the model loop and tools in-process and persists sessions itself.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Only one harness exists, so no two-harness operation; agent_dispatch can switch the model per subagent but all run the Crush loop.

limitations: Single embedded harness; no other coding-agent CLIs are controlled.

claims.answer: Routes: API keys for many providers, vendor model service Hyper (subscription and prepaid), ChatGPT subscription via OAuth against the Codex backend, GitHub Copilot and Grok account logins, and local models. Anthropic subscription login is not offered; Anthropic access is by API key. Account switching is by model or provider selection mid-session; no multi-account manager for one provider was found.

agent_subscriptions.answer: crush login supports ChatGPT (openai), GitHub Copilot and Grok accounts; no Claude Code or Gemini subscription login.

api_accounts.answer: Environment variables or the ctrl+l model picker take API keys for many providers.

vendor_credits.answer: Hyper is the official model provider with subscription and prepaid options (vendor claim); billing details unread.

local_models.answer: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, LiteLLM and oMLX discovery plus manual local model configuration.

account_switching.answer: Switch model and provider mid-session while preserving context; one stored credential per provider, no multi-account switching found in internal/config or oauth packages.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No vendor account is required; any API key or local model works. Hyper and subscription logins are optional.

provider_restrictions.answer: Provider terms for reusing subscription OAuth tokens (OpenAI, xAI, GitHub) are third-party policies not captured here.

limitations: No Claude subscription login; multiple accounts for one provider are not managed.
claims.unknownReason: Third-party provider terms about OAuth reuse are outside Crush public code.

claims.answer: Install via package manager, run crush, pick a model in the picker (Hyper login or API key) and start prompting; works in any directory with no Git requirement. Git features are only prompts to the model. No managed cloud or BYO-VPS installer exists.

first_task_setup.answer: Install, run crush, choose a model with ctrl+l (or set an API key env var), then prompt; crush runs with no config file.

no_git.answer: Works in any working directory; project context from files and optional /init; Git is not required by the agent loop (gitutil only reads branch names).

local_git_without_remote.answer: Git operations are plain shell commands in the local repo; no remote is required for commits.

hosted_git.answer: Commit and gh pr create instructions exist in the bash tool prompt, so GitHub use depends on the user having gh authenticated; no product-managed GitHub integration.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: README documents provider keys, clipboard tool prerequisites on Linux/BSD and trusted-config security notes.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: No managed cloud offering from Crush; Hyper is a model service only.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: crush server can run headless on a host, but there is no installer or onboarding flow for a VPS.

limitations: hosted_git: Commit and gh pr create instructions exist in the bash tool prompt, so GitHub use depends on the user having gh authenticated; no product-managed GitHub integration.
managed_cloud_setup: No managed cloud offering from Crush; Hyper is a model service only.
byo_vps_onboarding: crush server can run headless on a host, but there is no installer or onboarding flow for a VPS.

claims.answer: CLI: run (headless prompt), session list/show/last/delete/rename (json output), stats, logs, models. HTTP API from crush server with OpenAPI 3.1 docs covers workspaces, sessions, messages, agent run/cancel/queue/summarize, permissions, questions, MCP and config over unix socket or TCP; the handler has no authentication. No SDK, no webhook ingress and no MCP server exposing Crush to other agents.

api.answer: crush server serves a versioned /v1 HTTP API with OpenAPI docs.

sdk.answer: Bounded search of the repo for SDK packages (terms sdk, client library, npm package) found only the internal client used by the TUI.

mcp_server.answer: No command or package exposes Crush as an MCP server (searched cmd, server, backend for mcp serve/ServeMCP).

webhooks.answer: MCP channel pushes can inject messages into a session, but there is no generic inbound webhook endpoint.

operations.answer: API covers create/get/list sessions, post agent prompt, cancel, queue, summarize, shell, permission grant, question answer; stop is session cancel.

authentication.answer: Server handler chain has recover and logging only; searches for authorization, bearer, token and password in internal/server found no auth. Default is a unix socket.

stability.answer: /v1 prefix and OpenAPI document exist but no stability or deprecation policy is stated; pre-1.0 releases.

limitations: Server API has no authentication layer; no SDK; API stability is undocumented and the project is pre-1.0.

claims.answer: MCP client over http, stdio and sse with OAuth flow (including pre-registered clients), resources and prompts; Agent Skills from many directories (including .claude/skills and .cursor/skills); context files from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules and Copilot instructions; hooks for tool control; LSP integration. No plugin marketplace or custom Go tool plugin API.

mcp_client.answer: http, stdio and sse MCP servers, resources, prompts, per-server disable and Docker MCP enable endpoints.

plugins.answer: Bounded search found no plugin API or marketplace; extension points are MCP, skills and hooks.

custom_tools.answer: Custom tools only through MCP servers; hooks can rewrite tool input but not add tools.

instructions_import.answer: Reads AGENTS.md, CRUSH.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, .cursorrules and .github/copilot-instructions.md; skills from .claude, .cursor and .agents directories.

authentication.answer: MCP OAuth authorization-code flow with dynamic registration or pre-registered client credentials; static headers with shell expansion.

permission_scope.answer: Per-tool allow/deny (permissions allow/deny), MCP tools gated through the same permission prompts, and per-server tool disabling.

integration_owner.answer: Crush provides MCP client, skills and LSP itself; nothing is inherited from an underlying harness.

limitations: No plugin system beyond MCP, skills and hooks.

claims.answer: Single client implementation: a Go terminal UI built with Bubble Tea v2, Lip Gloss and Glamour. No desktop, mobile, Electron or web client.

desktop_implementation.answer: Terminal UI in Go using Bubble Tea v2; not a GUI app.

hybrids.answer: No hybrid or web-wrapped client in the pinned release.

implementation_evidence.answer: AGENTS.md architecture and internal/ui source at the pinned tag.

claims.answer: Intake is prompts typed in the TUI, piped stdin to crush run, API posts, and MCP channel pushes. No issue import, no tracker sync and no native chat or Git triggers.

local_creation.answer: Sessions (with todos) can be created locally, but there are no issue entities.

prompt_intake.answer: TUI prompt, crush run from args or stdin, server agent endpoint.

external_import.answer: No import command in cmd; trackers only through user-configured MCP servers.

chat_git_triggers.answer: MCP channels can push events into sessions; no Git or chat trigger is built in.

authoritative_tracker.answer: No tracker concept; sessions are the only durable objects.

stable_ids.answer: Session IDs and parent-session IDs are stable; there are no issue IDs.

sync.answer: No tracker sync code (searched linear, jira, github issue across internal).

external_roundtrips.answer: No native tracker to round-trip against.

limitations: No external tracker integration except through user-added MCP servers.

claims.answer: Crush has a plan agent and a todos tool that keep an in-session task list persisted on the session record; there are no acceptance criteria, plan editor or revision history.

plans.answer: A plan agent (read-only tools plus question) and a todos tool store a todo list on the session.

acceptance_criteria.answer: No acceptance-criteria field in the session schema or tools.

editors.answer: No plan editor; todos are written by the model through the todos tool.

revisions.answer: Todos overwrite; no revision history found in internal/session.

implementation_links.answer: Modified files per session are tracked, but not linked to a plan item.

amendment.answer: The user can steer or queue prompts during a run and the agent updates todos.

restart_persistence.answer: Sessions, messages and todos are stored in SQLite and resume with --continue/--session.

limitations: Todos are agent-maintained lists, not plans with revisions.

claims.answer: No epics or dependency graph. Parent-child exists only between a session and its subagent task sessions; blockers and readiness are not modelled.

epics.answer: No epic entity (Session has ParentSessionID for subagent task sessions only).

hierarchy.answer: Parent session to subagent session link; not user-managed work hierarchy.

task_to_epic.answer: No epic to promote a task to.

workflow_constraints.answer: No rigid workflow is required; the user can prompt freely.

limitations: epics: No epic entity (Session has ParentSessionID for subagent task sessions only).
hierarchy: Parent session to subagent session link; not user-managed work hierarchy.
blockers: No blocker field or tool.
readiness: No readiness concept.

claims.answer: Instruction files (AGENTS.md, CRUSH.md, CLAUDE.md and others, plus global CRUSH.md/AGENTS.md), Agent Skills, .crushignore and /init-generated context files. Cross-session memory is limited to those files and persisted sessions; there is no managed memory store.

instructions.answer: Project and global context files are added to the system prompt.

skills.answer: Agent Skills discovery from global and project directories with enable/disable.

project_docs.answer: Context paths can include directories of Markdown files; no docs indexing.

memory.answer: Bounded search (terms memory, remember) found no memory store; sessions and context files are the only continuity.

scope.answer: Global versus project scope for context files and skills is documented.

provenance.answer: No provenance or citation of context sources beyond the loaded file contents.

correction.answer: Context files are ordinary files the user edits; no correction workflow.

deletion.answer: Delete a file or session (crush session delete); no memory-specific deletion.

takeover_continuity.answer: A new client on the same crush server workspace shares sessions and history; otherwise only files and the local DB persist.

limitations: No managed memory with provenance, citation or stale-context controls.

claims.answer: Code navigation uses grep, glob, ls, view, Sourcegraph search and LSP tools (definitions, references, symbols, call hierarchy, diagnostics); web fetch and web search tools; image input depends on the model. No repository index, citations or architectural-conflict checks.

code_search.answer: grep, glob, ls, view, sourcegraph and LSP symbol tools.

indexing.answer: No repository index; search is live over files (searched index, embedding in internal).

external_knowledge.answer: fetch, web_fetch, web_search, sourcegraph and MCP resources.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Empty-media handling and file picker exist; image support depends on the chosen model.

freshness.answer: Live file reads are fresh; LSP state follows files; no freshness metadata for external sources.

access_scope.answer: .gitignore and .crushignore limit file listing; permissions gate tools.

api_retrieval.answer: No retrieval API beyond the agent tools and MCP resources.

citations.answer: No citation mechanism in tool outputs found.

limitations: No persistent index, retrieval API, citation or review-time enforcement.

claims.answer: No issue tracker. Sessions with titles and todos are listed and searchable in the session picker; there are no labels, assignees, priorities, archives or boards.

search.answer: Session picker lists sessions; no query language found.

filter.answer: No filters in session list command.

project_epic_views.answer: crush projects lists known projects; no epic views.

idea_parking.answer: No parking without starting a session.

metadata.answer: Title, token counts, cost, todos, channel.

durable_states.answer: No task states; only IsBusy runtime flag exposed by the server.

external_tracker_requirement.answer: An external tracker is required for any issue management; Crush has none.

limitations: A session list is not an issue tracker.

claims.answer: No shared issue records exist for agents to operate on; agents see only their todos tool and subagent tools.

read.answer: No issue read tool (bounded search of internal/agent/tools).

children.answer: agent_dispatch creates child subagent sessions, not issues.

results.answer: Subagent reports return to the parent session.

human_visibility.answer: Subagent sessions visible in the TUI transcript.

permissions.answer: Subagent write access is chosen per dispatch.

conflicts.answer: Prompt guidance asks for non-overlapping write scopes; nothing enforced.

limitations: shared_ids: No issue IDs.
read: No issue read tool (bounded search of internal/agent/tools).
create: No issue create tool.
update: No issue update tool.

claims.answer: No living product specification features; context files are static Markdown the user maintains.

persistent_requirements.answer: Context files persist instructions but are not requirement records.

agent_edits.answer: The agent can edit files like any other.

revisions.answer: No spec revision tracking beyond Git.

later_retrieval.answer: Context files are loaded at each session start.

limitations: persistent_requirements: Context files persist instructions but are not requirement records.
human_edits: Users edit files directly.
agent_edits: The agent can edit files like any other.
revisions: No spec revision tracking beyond Git.

claims.answer: Multiple sessions per project and multiple clients on one server workspace are supported; subagents can run concurrently; background shell jobs up to max_background_jobs (default 50). No documented quota on subagents. The server marks sessions IsBusy and counts attached clients.

concurrent_sessions.answer: Session picker, shared workspace with several clients, IsBusy per session.

concurrent_tasks.answer: agent_dispatch starts detached subagents that run in parallel with the parent.

quotas.answer: max_background_jobs (default 50) caps shell jobs; no subagent cap found in coordinator.go.

observed_concurrency.answer: Real-world concurrency is not measured in this catalog.

status_visibility.answer: Sessions show IsBusy and AttachedClients; subagent status via agent_status in transcript; no fleet view.

limitations: No concurrency quota for subagents; the TUI focuses one session at a time.
claims.unknownReason: Concurrency behavior in use is a runtime observation this catalog does not make.

claims.answer: No assignment, claims or queues for work. Prompts queue per session; routing exists only for MCP channel messages to a session.

agent_assignment.answer: The parent agent assigns a prompt to a labelled subagent.

claims.answer: No claims.

routing.answer: Channel messages are routed to one session per workspace.

duplicate_prevention.answer: Unique subagent names per session; no duplicate-work prevention.

limitations: human_assignment: No assignment concept.
agent_assignment: The parent agent assigns a prompt to a labelled subagent.
claims: No claims.
queues: Per-session prompt queue (queued prompts endpoints).

claims.answer: Product-owned delegation: the main agent can dispatch named subagents with read or write access and a chosen model, provider and reasoning effort, message them, stop them, check status, and receive their reports as later turns; subagents are persisted as sessions and reconciled after restart. In headless run mode delegation blocks. Cross-harness teams are not possible.

roles.answer: Read and write subagents with labels and generated names; plan and task agents.

model_harness_effort.answer: Model, provider and reasoning override per subagent; one harness.

messages.answer: agent_send follow-ups and reopen; reports back as subagent-report messages.

results_return.answer: Report folded into the next parent turn or starts a new turn.

orchestration_owner.answer: Product orchestration inside the Crush agent, not a provider-native or installed skill.

activation.answer: Available in the pinned release without a flag; headless run blocks instead of detaching.

authentication.answer: Subagents inherit the parent provider; permissions inherited from the session.

live_progress.answer: Subagent tool calls appear in the transcript; agent_status reports state.

retained_results.answer: Task sessions and reports are persisted in SQLite.

followup.answer: agent_send can restart a finished subagent (Reopened metadata).

invocation.answer: The model invokes agent_dispatch/agent tools; the user asks in natural language.

limitations: No cross-harness delegation; subagents cannot see the parent conversation.

claims.answer: No scheduler or recurring tasks. MCP servers opted in as channels can push events that start a turn in a session of a running server or TUI; there are no completion conditions or retries.

schedules.answer: Bounded search of cmd, agent and server for cron/schedule found no scheduler (hits are bash job or UI timing code).

events.answer: MCP channel pushes inject messages into a session, including on a headless server.

client_independence.answer: A headless crush server keeps routing channel pushes with no client attached.

limitations: Only MCP channel pushes can start work without a human prompt.

claims.answer: Cancel (esc/ctrl+c, API cancel), queued prompts as steering, permission prompts and question tool for decisions, stop of subagents, session resume. Pause is not offered distinct from cancel. Notifications for permission and turn end when unfocused.

pause.answer: No pause operation in the endpoint table; cancel only.

stop.answer: Agent session cancel endpoint; agent_stop for subagents; history preserved.

resume.answer: Resume a session by picker or --continue.

pending_decisions.answer: Permission queue and question tool surfaced in the UI and via API.

escalation.answer: Permission prompts escalate to the user; no timeouts or routing.

visible_errors.answer: Provider and tool errors appear in the transcript; logs via crush logs.

chat_terminal_parity.answer: Single terminal UI; run mode fixed so subagents no longer hang on prompts.

retained_history.answer: Messages persist in SQLite after cancel.

limitations: No pause; stop is cancel.

claims.answer: No fleet or epic management view; the session picker lists sessions and busy/attached signals.

parent_child.answer: Subagent sessions appear nested in the parent transcript.

attention.answer: Notifications and permission prompts; no cross-session attention inbox.

history.answer: Session list with history and messages.

workload.answer: Per-session tokens and cost in the sidebar; no workload view.

navigation_errors.answer: Errors are in each transcript only.

limitations: fleet_fixture: No fleet view.
parent_child: Subagent sessions appear nested in the parent transcript.
dependencies: No dependencies.
attention: Notifications and permission prompts; no cross-session attention inbox.

claims.answer: Free-form prompting with no mandatory workflow; subagent model and reasoning configurable per dispatch in natural language; roles and results visible in the transcript; no presets or epics.

quick_task.answer: Type a prompt or crush run.

presets.answer: Skills and the plan agent act as presets; no workflow presets.

natural_language.answer: Configuration through the built-in crush-config skill in natural language.

agent_configuration.answer: Per-subagent model, provider, reasoning and access.

in_run_changes.answer: Model, permission mode and queued prompts can change mid-session.

live_roles.answer: Subagent labels and names visible in the transcript.

discoverability.answer: Tool descriptions and README document delegation.

limitations: growing_epic: No epic entity.
presets: Skills and the plan agent act as presets; no workflow presets.
live_roles: Subagent labels and names visible in the transcript.

claims.answer: Executes on the machine running crush (or its server). A headless crush server on a user host can serve clients, but work does not move to a vendor cloud, and a closed terminal ends a TUI session while a server keeps running agents. No managed cloud.

local.answer: Agent loop and tools run in the local process.

byo_remote.answer: crush server can run on a remote host and clients can attach over tcp; the user sets it up and secures it (no auth).

self_hosted.answer: The server is a self-run service, but it is the same single-user backend and has no auth.

managed_cloud.answer: No Crush-operated compute; Hyper is inference only.

payer.answer: User pays for their own host and model usage.

client_disconnect.answer: A workspace is torn down when its last event stream disconnects (README); detached subagents keep running while the server lives.

other_device_continuation.answer: Another client on the same server and cwd can join the workspace and session.

limitations: No provisioning, vendor cloud or expiry model; remote means you run the server yourself.

claims.answer: Agents run on the user checkout with the user permissions; no worktree, branch, container, VM or OS sandbox is created by Crush. Isolation is the permission prompt system and tool allow/deny lists; the bash tool runs in a built-in shell interpreter on the host.

checkout.answer: Works in the project working directory.

branch.answer: No branch creation code (gitutil reads branch names only).

worktree.answer: Bounded search found no git worktree creation (2 doc-text hits only).

container.answer: No container runner; only a Docker MCP enable endpoint for MCP servers.

os_sandbox.answer: Searched firejail, bwrap, landlock, seccomp; none found.

filesystem.answer: .gitignore/.crushignore limit listing; tool permissions gate writes; no filesystem boundary.

process.answer: Shell tool runs host processes with background job limits.

network.answer: No network boundary beyond tool permissions.

secrets.answer: Config values can read env and 1Password via shell expansion; secrets are not isolated from the agent.

security_boundary.answer: README warns config is trusted code; yolo mode removes prompts.

limitations: Permission prompts are not a sandbox.

claims.answer: State persists in SQLite so transcripts, usage and todos survive crashes and restarts; subagents unanswered at shutdown are reported as interrupted; sessions resume via --continue; there is no process re-attachment or automatic task resumption.

client_disconnect.answer: Server keeps agents while any event stream remains; TUI exit cancels the run.

worker_crash.answer: DB state survives; in-flight run is lost.

service_restart.answer: Dispatches without reports are reconciled as interrupted on the next run.

process_reconnect.answer: No reattachment to running shell or agent processes.

task_resume.answer: Resume by prompting in the same session; subagents can be reopened with agent_send.

state_reconstruction.answer: Session record plus tracked files; no automatic repair.

context_loss.answer: Auto-summarize compacts context; summary replaces older messages.

duplicate_actions.answer: No guard against repeating a tool call after interruption.

manual_repair.answer: User retries manually; logs via crush logs.

multi_day_continuity.answer: Sessions persist across days in the local DB.

limitations: No process reconnection; interrupted subagents are reported, not auto-resumed.

claims.answer: Crush does not manage dependencies, caches, services, ports or secrets for workspaces; it uses the host environment and relies on LSP servers the user installs. Config supports env expansion.

services.answer: Starts LSP servers on demand; no app services.

secrets.answer: Env and command expansion in config values.

automatic_repair.answer: LSP restart tool; no environment repair.

limitations: dependencies: No dependency setup.
caches: No cache handling.
snapshots: No snapshots; per-file history only.
services: Starts LSP servers on demand; no app services.

claims.answer: Per-request inactivity timeout (default 60s, configurable), loop detection (repeated tool-call signature), auto-summarize on context pressure, background job cap. No turn, token or spend caps were found.

time_limits.answer: request_timeout aborts a stalled stream; no whole-run time limit.

turn_limits.answer: Loop detection stops repeated identical tool calls; no turn cap (searched max_turns, max_steps).

token_limits.answer: No token cap option in schema.json.

spend_limits.answer: No spend or budget option in schema.json.

timeouts.answer: request_timeout default 60s with first-token allowance; tool call timers.

retries.answer: Provider failure handling and stream stop fixes noted in release; retry policy not enumerated.

provider_failures.answer: StopFailure hook event and error display for provider errors.

enforcement.answer: Timeout and loop detection are enforced stops, not warnings.

limitations: No token, turn or spend limits.

claims.answer: Logs (crush logs, ./.crush/logs), session cost/token tracking, crush stats with usage by day, model, hour and tool, tool call timers. No traces, per-agent or per-project dashboards beyond stats --all, and no performance measurement.

logs.answer: crush logs with tail and follow; --debug.

traces.answer: No tracing/OTEL export found (4 incidental hits).

failure_reasons.answer: Errors in transcript and logs; StopFailure hook.

usage_export.answer: crush stats renders an HTML report; session show supports json.

agent_stats.answer: Stats by model and tool, not by agent role.

time_stats.answer: Usage by day, hour and weekday.

failure_status.answer: Failed tool calls shown in transcript.

approval_status.answer: Pending permission requests exposed in UI and API.

reconnect_consistency.answer: Server events stream; state in SQLite.

performance_method.answer: This catalog measures no speed figures; see ADEMark if listed.

limitations: No traces or usage export format beyond stats HTML.

claims.answer: Session cost in USD is shown in the sidebar and stored per session using catalog pricing or provider-reported cost (OpenRouter), with token counts and an estimated-usage flag; subagent task sessions are separate sessions. No epic aggregation, budgets or alerts; subscription logins do not report marginal cost.

child_cost.answer: Child task sessions hold their own cost; parent aggregation not confirmed.

billed_vs_estimated.answer: EstimatedUsage flag distinguishes estimated token usage; cost derives from pricing or provider metadata.

tokens.answer: Prompt and completion tokens per session.

provider_reconciliation.answer: Uses OpenRouter-reported cost when present; no reconciliation to invoices.

export.answer: stats report and session JSON output.

limitations: No budgets, alerts or export of per-task cost beyond stats.

claims.answer: No compute-aware scheduling. Background shell jobs are capped (max_background_jobs); prompts queue per session; no CPU/RAM awareness or check deduplication.

cancellation.answer: Cancel a session or a subagent; kill background jobs with job_kill.

limitations: concurrency: max_background_jobs cap for shell jobs.
queues: Per-session prompt queue.
cpu_ram: No CPU/RAM limits.
backpressure: None found.

claims.answer: Several clients with the same --cwd join one server workspace and share session list, history, permission queue, LSP and MCP state, and a session mirrors live in all attached clients, but there are no accounts, comments or presence beyond an attached-client count. Co-prompting is possible in the same session through any attached client without attribution.

visibility.answer: Attached clients mirror the same session live.

discussion.answer: No discussion thread beyond the transcript.

coprompting.answer: Any attached client can post prompts to the shared session; queue ordering applies.

owner_online.answer: The server host must be running; clients can attach and detach.

limitations: No identity, comments, presence or permissions; server API is unauthenticated.

claims.answer: No organization, project or task roles, membership, SSO or provisioning; the server has no authentication.

organization_roles.answer: Bounded search of internal for rbac, organization, sso, saml found none relevant.

unauthorized_access.answer: Server handler has no auth; access control is the unix socket file permissions or network placement.

limitations: organization_roles: Bounded search of internal for rbac, organization, sso, saml found none relevant.
project_roles: None.
task_roles: None.
membership: None.

claims.answer: Per-tool-call permission prompts with allow once, allow for session and deny; persistent allow/deny lists by tool name in config; bash read-only commands auto-allowed after parsing; yolo mode skips prompts but refuses dangerous commands; PreToolUse hooks can allow/deny or rewrite. These are product-enforced in the tool layer.

command.answer: Bash command permission with parsed read-only auto-allow.

network.answer: fetch/web tools are permission-gated tools; no network policy.

delivery.answer: No delivery approval; commit/push are bash commands behind prompts.

revoke.answer: Edit config lists; session grants end with the session.

defaults.answer: Default asks before tool calls; yolo is opt-in via --yolo.

enforcement.answer: Enforced in the hooked tool decorator and permission service, not prompt-only.

limitations: No network, secret or delivery approvals; default mode asks per tool call.

evidence.locator: LICENSE.md: Abbreviation, License Grant, Permitted Purpose, Future License
evidence.finding: Functional Source License 1.1 with MIT Future License: use, copy, modify and redistribute for any Permitted Purpose except a Competing Use; each version converts to MIT after the stated period. Source-available, not a standard OSI license today.

evidence.title: AGENTS.md development guide
evidence.finding: Package map: app wiring, cmd, config, agent (SessionAgent, coordinator), hooks, session (SQLite), lsp, ui (Bubble Tea v2), permission, skills, shell, event (PostHog), pubsub; context files AGENTS.md/CRUSH.md/CLAUDE.md/GEMINI.md read from the working directory.

evidence.title: Config JSON schema
evidence.locator: schema.json $defs Options, Permissions, MCPConfig, SelectedModel, Pricing
evidence.finding: Options include request_timeout, max_background_jobs, disable_auto_summarize, disable_metrics, disabled_tools, attribution, notifications, context_paths, skills_paths; MCP config includes channel_enabled and oauth; no budget, turn or spend-limit option.

evidence.title: CLI root command and metrics gate
evidence.locator: internal/cmd/root.go (command registration; CRUSH_DISABLE_METRICS and DO_NOT_TRACK checks near line 984)
evidence.finding: Registered commands: run, server, login, logout, logs, models, projects, session (list/show/last/delete/rename), stats, dirs, schema, update-providers. No scheduler, issue, export or MCP-serve command. Metrics disabled by CRUSH_DISABLE_METRICS or DO_NOT_TRACK.

evidence.title: crush login command
evidence.locator: internal/cmd/login.go Long help and platform switch
evidence.finding: Login platforms: hyper, copilot (github-copilot), openai/chatgpt, grok (xai). No Claude subscription login.

evidence.title: ChatGPT OAuth against the Codex backend
evidence.finding: PKCE browser flow lets a ChatGPT account use its subscription through chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex (same flow as Codex CLI).

evidence.title: Grok/xAI OAuth
evidence.finding: Sign in with the Grok account its subscription is attached to; access token is a Bearer credential for api.x.ai/v1.

evidence.title: GitHub Copilot device-flow login
evidence.finding: GitHub device-code flow exchanged for a Copilot token via api.github.com/copilot_internal/v2/token; subscription reuse.

evidence.title: crush server command
evidence.finding: crush server serves the HTTP API over unix socket (default), tcp or http host; OpenAPI 3.1 docs at /v1/docs/; SIGHUP reloads config.

evidence.title: Server construction and handler
evidence.finding: Plain http.ServeMux over unix or tcp listener with recover and logging middleware; no authentication or TLS middleware in the handler chain (search terms: authorization, bearer, token, password in internal/server).

evidence.title: Server HTTP endpoint table
evidence.finding: Endpoints for workspaces, sessions, messages, agent run/cancel/queue/summarize/shell, permissions grant and mode, questions, MCP state and auth, LSP, config, skills, events (SSE), git branch.

evidence.title: crush run non-interactive command
evidence.finding: Single prompt headless run from args or stdin with --model, --small-model, --reasoning-effort, --session, --continue, --quiet, --verbose; attaches to a running server when one exists.

evidence.title: agent_dispatch subagent tools
evidence.finding: agent_dispatch starts a detached subagent with label, read/write access and optional model/provider/reasoning override; agent_send follows up or reopens; agent_stop stops; reports arrive as later turns.

evidence.title: agent_dispatch tool description
evidence.finding: Subagent reports back as a <subagent-report>; agent_status/agent_send/agent_stop address it by unique name; subagents keep running if the user interrupts; write subagents should use non-overlapping scopes.

evidence.title: Coordinator and subagent runtime
evidence.locator: internal/agent/coordinator.go dispatched map, runReport, reconciled, effectiveToolNames
evidence.finding: Coordinator tracks detached subagents per parent session, folds reports into turns, reconciles unanswered dispatches as interrupted after restart; blocking subagent calls move to background after 60s; tool events fire only for the top-level agent.

evidence.title: Permission service
evidence.finding: Per-tool-call prompts with allow, allow-for-session and deny; permission modes include yolo (never prompts, refuses dangerous commands); subagents inherit session auto-approval.

evidence.title: Crush hooks guide
evidence.locator: docs/hooks/README.md Events table and Execution model
evidence.finding: 13 hook events (PreToolUse can allow/deny/rewrite, PostToolUse, TurnStart/End, SessionStart/End, PreCompact...) running user shell commands; Claude Code compatible payloads; hooks fire for the top-level agent only.

evidence.title: crush stats command
evidence.finding: Usage statistics by day, model, hour, weekday, tool, with total tokens and cost across sessions or all known projects; renders an HTML report.

evidence.title: Session model
evidence.finding: SQLite-backed session with ParentSessionID, token counts, Cost, Todos, Channel; task sessions for subagents.

evidence.title: Telemetry events
evidence.finding: PostHog events: app initialized/exited, session created/deleted, prompt sent/responded, tokens used, stats viewed; pseudonymous device hash.

evidence.title: Bash tool prompt (git commit and PR)
evidence.finding: Prompt instructs the model to create commits with attribution trailers and PRs via gh pr create; no product-native PR object, only the bash tool and the gh CLI.

evidence.title: Built-in tool set

evidence.finding: File, shell, search, LSP, web and MCP-resource tools; no dedicated git, PR, worktree, container or screenshot tool.

evidence.title: MCP channel router
evidence.finding: MCP servers opted in via --channels or channel_enabled can push messages that the server injects into exactly one session per workspace, even with no client attached; reply routing via channel_reply.

evidence.title: herdr status integration
evidence.finding: When run inside a herdr pane, reports idle/working/blocked state over herdr Unix socket API.

evidence.title: Loop detection
evidence.finding: Stops a run when a tool-call signature repeats more than 5 times in a 10-step window.

evidence.title: Session agent run loop
evidence.finding: Auto-summarizes when remaining context falls under a threshold unless disabled; per-step usage updates session tokens and cost (OpenRouter-reported or catalog pricing).
